Invariant improved: Exact intake set and mutation detection
Candidate: Merkleized intake manifest over canonical occurrence records
Conventional alternative: Flat sorted manifest with one SHA-256 digest
Why alternative may be insufficient: Large generations require full-manifest rehash for localized verification/resume.
Runtime/resource effect: Additional hashes and storage; faster subtree verification only if exploited.
Failure modes: Tree canonicalization drift, omitted leaf fields, incompatible proof versions.
Observability: Leaf/node counts, build time, proof failures, manifest/root digest.
Compatibility: Optional internal format behind IntakeGeneration schema; flat canonical export retained.
Falsification benchmark: Compare build/update/resume verification time and bytes for 10k/100k/1m entries; reject if gain is immaterial.

Invariant improved: Canonical exact-byte identity with efficient hashing
Candidate: BLAKE3 streaming acceleration alongside mandatory SHA-256
Why alternative may be insufficient: CPU-bound hashing on fast storage may limit throughput.
Complexity cost: Low-medium; dual digest/versioning and dependency provenance.
Runtime/resource effect: More digest metadata; possible CPU reduction only if SHA-256 strategy is optimized/parallelized safely.
Failure modes: Treating BLAKE3 as canonical, digest mismatch, platform implementation drift.
Compatibility: SHA-256 remains canonical and public; BLAKE3 optional derived field.
Falsification benchmark: Large-file and small-file hashing on native platforms; reject if total pipeline gain is negligible.

Conventional alternative: Resolve/canonicalize path then reopen by path
Why alternative may be insufficient: Paths can be replaced between validation and use.
Runtime/resource effect: More open handles and metadata checks; fewer redundant path walks.
Failure modes: Handle leaks, unsupported filesystems, platform semantic mismatch.
Observability: Open/close counts, native object IDs, mutation rejection reasons, handle leaks.
Compatibility: Public paths remain locators; internal SourceAccess contract changes.
Falsification benchmark: Barrier-driven mutation corpus plus overhead measurement; reject unsafe fallback.

Candidate: Phase-internal durable WorkItems with one phase barrier
Why alternative may be insufficient: Hashing/analysis can underutilize resources and lose granular recovery.
Complexity cost: Medium-high; work state, retries, aggregation, budgets.
Runtime/resource effect: Higher throughput and DB/event volume; bounded queues required.
Failure modes: Cross-phase leakage, duplicate work, unfairness, non-deterministic aggregation.
Observability: Queue depth, active work, retries, barrier closure, resource reservations.
Compatibility: Six phase order unchanged; legacy phase adapter may execute one work item.
Falsification benchmark: Representative hashing/analyzer workloads; reject if overhead exceeds gain or recovery worsens.

Why alternative may be insufficient: Duplicate content and expensive analyzers repeat identical work.
Runtime/resource effect: Storage/lookup cost in exchange for avoided CPU/I/O.
Failure modes: Omitted key dimension causes stale result; provenance loss.
Observability: Hit/miss reason, full key digest, work avoided, semantic comparison.
Compatibility: Optional optimization; recompute fallback always valid.
Falsification benchmark: Duplicate-heavy runs with deliberate config/policy/tool changes; reject unsafe or low-value reuse.

Candidate: Explicit single-writer transaction owner with WAL/reference backend
Why alternative may be insufficient: Write contention and transaction ownership become ambiguous.
Complexity cost: Medium; queue/transaction API and shutdown behavior.
Runtime/resource effect: May batch writes and reduce locks; single-writer bottleneck possible.
Failure modes: Writer stall/backlog, oversized transaction, shutdown loss.
Observability: Queue depth, transaction latency, busy time, batch size, fsync time.
Compatibility: StateStore interface hides implementation; schema unchanged by writer topology.
Falsification benchmark: Concurrent-job and event workloads; reject if tail latency/backlog is worse without reliability gain.

Candidate: Sampled/coalesced progress plus authoritative checkpoint state
Why alternative may be insufficient: High-volume files produce excessive DB/outbox/event pressure.
Complexity cost: Low-medium; sampling policy and status projection.
Runtime/resource effect: Lower writes/events; slightly less granular history.
Failure modes: Hidden stalls, final progress not flushed, misleading percentages.
Compatibility: Event schema/version documents sampling; status remains authoritative.
Falsification benchmark: Million-entry/event-surge workloads; reject policy that harms diagnostics or recovery.

Candidate: Stage → hash/verify → fsync as policy → atomic no-replace commit
Conventional alternative: Write directly to final digest path
Why alternative may be insufficient: Partial/crashed/concurrent writes can corrupt trusted blob.
Runtime/resource effect: Extra temporary bytes and verification I/O.
Failure modes: Orphan stages, cross-device rename, corrupt pre-existing object.
Observability: Stage state, bytes, digest, commit conflict, reconciliation action.
Falsification benchmark: Concurrent writers and crash matrix; direct-write alternative fails safety invariant.

Why alternative may be insufficient: Crash/failure can produce state without history or published event without committed state.
Runtime/resource effect: Additional DB writes/storage; asynchronous delivery improves availability.
Failure modes: Backlog, duplicate delivery, poison messages, stale dispatcher.
Observability: State/event/outbox transaction IDs, backlog depth/age, attempts, DLQ.
Compatibility: Existing event bus becomes transport adapter; event consumers versioned.
Falsification benchmark: Every commit/crash boundary; reject any design permitting unpaired authoritative state/event.

Invariant improved: Detection of concurrency/state defects before runtime
Candidate: Bounded model checking with executable counterexample replay
Why alternative may be insufficient: Rare interleavings across lease/fence/control/crash may be missed.
Runtime/resource effect: CI analysis cost only; no product runtime effect.
Failure modes: False assurance, state-space explosion, model drift.
Observability: States explored, bounds, runtime, counterexamples, replay status.
Falsification benchmark: Seed deliberate defects and measure unique defects found/maintenance; retire if no added value.

Candidate: Remote ExecutionBackend using immutable WorkSpec, leases, fences, and scoped artifact tokens
Why alternative may be insufficient: Some workloads may exceed one host or need specialized tools.
Complexity cost: Very high; identity, transport, worker ops, partitions, upgrades.
Runtime/resource effect: Transfer/queue overhead and new operational services; possible throughput gains.
Failure modes: Partition, stale worker, forged result, duplicate work, version skew, data exposure.
Observability: Lease/fence, protocol versions, transfer, queue, worker health, result validation.
Compatibility: Optional backend; local reference path remains required.
Falsification benchmark: Defined workload versus local including operator burden; reject without measurable benefit.

Invariant improved: Fast local verification of large manifests
Candidate: Sparse status/materialized projections and paginated lineage queries
Conventional alternative: Load complete metadata/finding/event JSON into job record
Why alternative may be insufficient: Large jobs cause memory, serialization, and status latency amplification.
Complexity cost: Medium; normalized records and projection/version contract.
Runtime/resource effect: More indexed tables; lower memory/JSON transfer.
Failure modes: Projection lag/inconsistency, missing pagination ordering, N+1 queries.
Observability: Query latency, rows/bytes, projection version, stale indicator.
Compatibility: Legacy metadata view generated during migration window.
Falsification benchmark: Large-history status workloads with exact state/lineage equivalence.
